newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu leaves France to face Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu leaves France to face Zaire crisis.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko left France for his battered homeland on Tuesday after four months in Europe recuperating from cancer surgery.

Mobutu's jet took off from Nice airport at 8.50 a.m. (0750 GMT), about an hour later than planned, as the president prepared to face a Tustsi rebellion in the east of his sprawling country that poses the biggest challenge to his 31-year-rule.

Supporters of Africa's longest-serving strongman were planning a mammoth welcome on Tuesday afternoon in Kinshasa, depicting Mobutu as a saviour after Rwandan-backed rebels seized a swathe of territory around the Great Lakes.

Mobutu, 66, flew home aboard a special DC-8 plane, accompanied by a cargo plane and several private jets. He and his entourage arrived at Nice airport for the seven-hour flight in three Mercedes cars, four minibuses and a taxi.
Airport workers were seen loading washing machines, televisions and video recorders into one of the planes.
Aides say the president, in power since 1965, is feeling better after surgery for prostate cancer in Switzerland in August, although other witnesses have described him as looking tired and drawn.

One Zairean newspaper said he planned to stay in Zaire just two or three weeks before returning to complete his convalescence in his villa at Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, overlooking the Mediterranean, where he had been staying since November 4.

Mobutu has give little hint of how he aims to solve the Tutsi rebellion in eastern Zaire. The rebel coalition has overwhelmed Zaire's ragged army in a two-month offensive, taking several key towns including Goma, Bukavu and Uvira.

In Nairobi on Tuesday, eight African leaders called after a one-day summit for the warring parties in eastern Zaire to agree to a negotiated peaceful settlement, state-run Kenya radio said. Zaire did not attend the meeting.
Zairean newspapers debated whether Mobutu would seek to negotiate an end to the conflict or reassemble the defeated army for a counteroffensive against the Tutsi-led rebels.
About 600,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees were forced by the fighting in eastern Zaire to return last month to the country they fled in 1994.
The Zairean leader has stayed closeted inside his villa, apart from a visit to a doctor, meeting African leaders and U.N. envoy Raymond Chretien.

France, a long-time ally, showed little embarrassment at the veteran leader's extended stay. By contrast, Switzerland said last month it had denied a visa to him when he asked to return for new medical treatment.

Mobutu returned to favour in France after cooperating with a 1994 French military expedition aimed at helping prevent genocide in neighbouring Rwanda. His star rose further with the return of the Gaullists to the French presidency with Jacques Chirac's victory last year.

The only serious incident during Mobutu's stay in France was a road accident in nearby Menton when the Zairean ambassador to Paris, Ramazani Baya, ran over and killed two schoolboys on a pedestrian crossing.
Police said Baya was driving at 100 kph (62 mph) in a 45-kph (30-mph) zone. Mobutu has agreed to strip Baya of his diplomatic immunity so that he can stand trial, but that has not yet occurred.
